source: KCC 2026/27 budget pack (ModernGov 12 Feb 2026 County Council; main report s134609 + Appendix D s134613 + Appendix F s134615), verified figure-by-figure. Supersedes the prior 2024/25 figures.

directorates.name: Adult Social Care & Health (ASCH)
directorates._note: 47.8% of net budget, the largest ASC share in the focus set.

cross_cutting._note: The 2026/27 savings programme is GBP 87.6m gross for in-year delivery, GBP 47.6m net new savings and income. By directorate (gross additional): ASC GBP 30m, Children's GBP 18m, other services GBP 27.6m (across GET, CED and corporate).

reserves._note: General reserve target 5 to 10 percent of net budget. The 2026/27 budget is balanced with GBP 25m of one-offs (GBP 9m capital receipts flexibility + GBP 16m earmarked reserves release). Usable reserves total to-populate from the budget pack.

risks.risk: Adult Social Care overspend of about GBP 45m (2024/25) rising to about GBP 50.9m mid-year 2025/26; ASC is GBP 89.8m of the GBP 178m total spending growth.
DSG / SEND accumulated deficit of about GBP 136m by end 2025/26, held off the General Fund by a statutory override that ends 31 March 2028.
ASC books about GBP 30m of new savings but net of GBP 18.3m of reversals of unachievable prior savings, a 61 percent write-off that signals delivery risk on the ASC programme.
The 2026/27 budget is balanced with GBP 25m of one-offs that need replacing with sustainable savings in future years.
MTFP gap of GBP 54.2m (2027/28) and GBP 42.1m (2028/29), assuming nil council-tax increase in planning years.

asc_chc_position.metric: NHS Continuing Healthcare eligibility (snapshot, not spend)
asc_chc_position.source: NHS England Continuing Healthcare and NHS-funded Nursing Care CSV, 2025/26 Q4.
asc_chc_position.note: Kent and Medway ICB is above the England median on CHC eligibility (rank 10 of 42), so the CHC funding share is a cost-shift exposure to DEFEND against NHS tightening, not an under-claiming saving to recover. Mirrors the June 2026 Lancashire CHC correction (L&SC ICB 79.8, rank 3 of 42). Kent and Medway is a single ICB / sub-ICB footprint that also covers Medway unitary; there is no Medway-separable sub-ICB, so any Kent-CC-only exposure figure needs a district-level package base before it is quoted.
